standard.title: Create texts for diverse audiences
standard.description: create spoken, written and multimodal, informative and imaginative texts, selecting vocabulary, expressions, grammatical structures and textual conventions for familiar and some unfamiliar contexts and purposes, to engage different audiences
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can create spoken, written and multimodal texts using appropriate vocabulary, grammar and some textual conventions (AC9LS8EC06). They have not yet created texts for deliberately varied or unfamiliar audiences, or made strategic language selections to engage different audiences across different contexts and purposes.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students create spoken, written and multimodal texts (informative and imaginative) in the target language for familiar and some unfamiliar contexts, making deliberate selections of vocabulary, expressions, grammatical structures and textual conventions to engage different audiences.

nodes.label: Creating for a specific audience
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can make deliberate language and textual decisions in a target language text based on a clearly identified audience.
nodes.minimum_width: Produce one target language text where at least two deliberate choices (vocabulary, structure, register, format) are explicitly made with reference to audience.
nodes.typical_width: Create informative and imaginative texts with a clearly identified audience; make deliberate vocabulary, register and format choices that reflect audience knowledge, expectations and needs; produce bilingual texts for mixed-language audiences where appropriate.
wider: Create the same content for two significantly different audiences (e.g. peers vs community members; second language learners vs fluent speakers) — compare the language choices required for each
Produce a promotional or community text in the target language for a real audience — evaluate its effectiveness based on actual reception
nodes.hinge_reason: Audience-oriented text creation is the central move of EC06 at Y9-10 — it distinguishes text creation from language practice. Students who produce target language texts without reference to audience are still doing EC06 Y7-8 tasks. The entire descriptor's demand for 'engaging different audiences' collapses if audience awareness is not established as a production criterion.

response_modes.reason: Audience awareness in production requires students to hold a mental model of the reader or viewer while making language choices — a metacognitive demand that requires explicit scaffolding. Audience analysis tasks and annotation of deliberate choices make the process visible.

success_criteria: Produces a text where at least two deliberate language choices are explicitly justified with reference to audience
Can explain how a different audience would require different language or format choices for the same content

nodes.label: Selecting vocabulary and grammar for effect
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can select vocabulary, expressions and grammatical structures in the target language to achieve a specific communicative effect, purpose or tone.
nodes.minimum_width: Demonstrate at least two deliberate vocabulary or grammar selections in a text that are explained with reference to intended effect or purpose.
nodes.typical_width: Select vocabulary and grammatical structures purposefully for register, tone and effect; use a range of text types (presentation, narrative, promotional, reflective, persuasive) with appropriate conventions; experiment with creative language features (rhyme, repetition, imagery) in imaginative texts.
wider: Revise a draft text with a focus on vocabulary and grammar for effect — compare before and after versions and evaluate the changes
Experiment with poetic or rhetorical devices from target language literary or oral traditions — identify the effect of each device and discuss its cultural resonance

response_modes.reason: Strategic selection requires having encountered vocabulary and grammar across enough registers and text types to have genuine choices. Students who have only practised one register cannot select — they default. Varied production contexts across registers and purposes build the repertoire from which selection is possible.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Strategic language selection for effect is where students demonstrate genuine communicative competence — the ability to shape language, not just use it. This is the highest-value indicator of progress in the creating strand at Y9-10.
success_criteria: Demonstrates at least two deliberate vocabulary or grammar choices in a text and can explain their intended effect
Produces texts in at least two different registers or text types with appropriate conventions for each

nodes.label: Creating imaginative texts with creative intent
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can create imaginative texts in the target language with deliberate creative intent — making choices that produce a specific emotional, humorous or aesthetic effect on an audience.
nodes.minimum_width: Produce one imaginative text in the target language with at least one deliberate creative choice (structural, linguistic or thematic) and explain its intended effect.
nodes.typical_width: Create imaginative texts across formats (narrative, performance, poem, script) with deliberate creative choices; adapt familiar stories or characters for new purposes or audiences; use creative language features; produce texts designed to entertain, provoke or engage a specific audience.
wider: Adapt a familiar cultural story or text from the target language community for a different audience or purpose — discuss what is retained, changed and why
Create a collaborative imaginative text with a peer — negotiate creative choices and reflect on how collaboration shaped the final product

response_modes.reason: Imaginative text creation with deliberate creative intent integrates audience awareness (node 1), vocabulary and grammar selection (node 2), and knowledge of target language textual conventions into a purposeful creative act. Performance, presentation and peer response contexts are the natural integration structure.

success_criteria: Produces an imaginative text with at least one deliberate creative choice that is explained with reference to intended audience effect
Text demonstrates awareness of target language textual conventions for the chosen format
